rationale: A retry limit above 5 disables back-off, retries retain the original inputs, and an ultimate failure in a pinned lane fails the whole run.

stem: A tile failed with an outdated input, and the upstream value has since been corrected. The next execution must use the corrected value. What should the operator do?
options: {'A': 'Increase the retry limit so a later retry refreshes its inputs.', 'B': 'Enable retry back-off so the retry reads the upstream value again.', 'C': 'Start a new tile execution with newly captured inputs instead of relying on a retry.', 'D': 'Pin the lane so the existing retry inherits the corrected input.'}
rationale: Retries always reuse the original inputs, so a new tile execution is required to capture the corrected upstream value.

stem: An underscore lane must run on every beat for 20 beats and needs three tiles active throughout. Which setup meets the requirement?
options: {'A': 'Pin the lane, keep it at three tiles, and renew the pin before each 12-beat expiration.', 'B': 'Leave the lane unpinned with three tiles because underscore lanes run automatically when they are not full.', 'C': 'Pin the lane with four tiles and allow the fourth tile to wait until the first pin expires.', 'D': 'Pin the lane once because a pin remains active until the run ends.'}
rationale: An underscore lane must be pinned to run, a pinned lane supports at most three tiles, and its pin must be renewed before 12 beats elapse.

stem: An underscore lane ran on every beat after being pinned but stopped after 12 beats, with no upgrade or tile failure occurring. What is the most likely explanation?
options: {'A': 'The scheduler hid the lane because it contained fewer than seven tiles.', 'B': 'The pin expired because it was not renewed.', 'C': 'The lane was automatically split after 12 beats.', 'D': 'The scheduler paused the lane for retry back-off.'}
rationale: Pins expire after 12 beats unless renewed, and an underscore lane does not run without a pin.

stem: Two lanes each contain three tiles and run for the same beats, and all six tiles can operate correctly in one shared lane. Which change reduces billing weight without removing any tiles?
options: {'A': 'Run ledger compact after every beat.', 'B': 'Split each lane into two smaller lanes.', 'C': 'Enable eager mode on a ferry between the lanes.', 'D': 'Merge the two half-full lanes into one lane.'}
rationale: Merging two half-full lanes reduces billing weight, while compaction does not affect weight, splitting does not reduce it, and eager mode increases receiving-lane weight.

stem: Which operator assumption about Tessellate billing is mistaken?
options: {'A': 'Idle tiles in a running lane still contribute to billing weight.', 'B': 'Billing weight depends on the number of tiles and the beats run.', 'C': 'Running ledger compact reduces billing weight as well as stored history.', 'D': 'Merging two half-full lanes can reduce billing weight.'}
rationale: Ledger compact reduces stored history but does not reduce billing weight.

stem: A lane already contains seven tiles when an operator submits an eighth tile to it. What happens to the eighth tile?
options: {'A': 'It is silently queued rather than rejected.', 'B': 'It replaces the oldest tile in the lane.', 'C': 'It is automatically moved to a new lane.', 'D': 'It starts immediately while an idle tile is removed.'}
rationale: A lane holds at most seven tiles, and an eighth tile is silently queued.

stem: Four producer tiles and three consumer tiles must directly share memory without using a ferry, while an eighth independent tile must also be able to run without waiting in the same lane's queue. Which layout meets these requirements?
options: {'A': 'Place all eight tiles in one normal lane.', 'B': 'Place the four producers in one normal lane and the three consumers in another, with the independent tile in either lane.', 'C': 'Place the seven producers and consumers together in one normal lane, and place the independent tile in a second normal lane.', 'D': 'Place the seven producers and consumers in an unpinned underscore lane, and place the independent tile in a normal lane.'}
rationale: Tiles that need shared memory must share one lane, seven fit within its capacity, and the independent eighth tile can run from another scheduler-visible lane.

stem: A gate is checked at the start of every beat. Its condition becomes true immediately after the check on beat 6 and remains true. When is the blocked tile first able to proceed?
options: {'A': 'Immediately after the condition becomes true on beat 6', 'B': 'At the gate check on beat 7', 'C': 'At the gate check on beat 10', 'D': 'After three additional retry attempts'}
rationale: Gates are checked only once per beat, so a condition that becomes true after beat 6's check is first recognized on beat 7.

stem: A tile passed a gate on beat 4, and a snapshot was taken on beat 6. The gate condition later became false. After the snapshot is restored, the tile is blocked at the same gate even though it had previously passed it. What is the cause?
options: {'A': 'Restoring a snapshot re-runs gates from scratch, and the condition is now false', 'B': 'The snapshot omitted the tile because gated tiles are stored only in ferries', 'C': 'The restore changed the gate into a retry operation', 'D': 'Gates are permanently closed after six beats'}
rationale: A snapshot restore re-runs gates from scratch, so a previously passed tile can block if the gate condition is no longer true.

stem: One reader tile must read every lane, including underscore lanes, but four unrelated tiles must not receive that access. All five tiles currently share the `reports` lane. Which change satisfies the requirement with the least access?
options: {'A': 'Grant the `reports` lane the `wide` scope and leave all five tiles there', 'B': 'Move the reader tile to a dedicated lane and grant only that lane the `wide` scope', 'C': 'Grant the reader tile a narrower scope than the `reports` lane', 'D': 'Rename every underscore lane so that no special scope is required'}
rationale: Permissions are inherited from lanes, so isolating the reader in a dedicated `wide` lane avoids granting the same access to unrelated tiles.

stem: A lane contains a diagnostic tile and three ordinary processing tiles. An operator grants the lane the `wide` scope solely so the diagnostic tile can inspect every lane. What is over-broad about this configuration?
options: {'A': 'The `wide` scope doubles the billing weight of all four tiles', 'B': 'The `wide` scope automatically pins every lane it can read', 'C': 'All four tiles inherit `wide` access from the lane, not just the diagnostic tile', 'D': 'All four tiles become able to bypass gates continuously'}
rationale: Permissions are inherited from the lane, so every tile in the lane receives the `wide` scope.

stem: At snapshot time, lane memory contains `count = 12`, a ferry carrying `record X` is in transit to that lane, and a tile has already passed a gate. What should an operator expect after restoring the snapshot?
options: {'A': 'The count and in-transit record are restored, and the gate remains passed', 'B': 'The count is restored, the in-transit record is not restored, and the gate is evaluated again', 'C': 'Only the in-transit record is restored, and the gate is removed', 'D': 'Nothing is restored because snapshots capture only tile definitions'}
rationale: Snapshots capture lane memory but not in-transit ferry contents, and restoring them causes gates to run again from scratch.

stem: Data was sent through a ferry but had not arrived when a snapshot was taken. After restoring that snapshot, the destination lane never receives the data. What best explains the loss?
options: {'A': 'Snapshots exclude ferry contents that are in transit', 'B': 'Snapshots discard all lane memory created before the current beat', 'C': 'Ferries stop permanently whenever any snapshot is restored', 'D': 'Restoring a snapshot reduces every ferry to a 2 MB limit'}
rationale: A snapshot does not capture ferry contents in transit, so that data is unavailable after the restore.

stem: A tile computes an incorrect candidate output and then fails. The operator needs to inspect that output, but enabling `trace` shows only the tile's inputs. Which approach can capture the candidate output?
options: {'A': 'Enable `trace` twice so that the second trace records outputs', 'B': 'Wait for the fifth-beat metric sample, which records complete tile outputs', 'C': 'Set `ferry.eager = true`, which adds outputs to the trace', 'D': 'Instrument the tile to save the candidate output into lane memory before failing, then capture that memory in a snapshot'}
rationale: The `trace` flag never records outputs, so the output must be explicitly stored elsewhere, such as lane memory captured by a snapshot.

stem: A metric briefly spikes on beats 11 through 14 and returns to normal before beat 15. No spike appears in the recorded metrics. Why?
options: {'A': 'Metrics are sampled only on every fifth beat, so the spike occurred entirely between samples', 'B': 'Metrics ignore activity lasting fewer than five seconds', 'C': 'Metrics are recorded only for pinned lanes', 'D': 'A metric is discarded whenever a gate is evaluated'}
rationale: Metrics are sampled on beats 5, 10, 15, and so on, and events occurring only between those samples are not recorded.

stem: The underscore lane `_audit` is pinned and running before a Tessellate upgrade. Its pin is not recreated after the upgrade. What will happen to the lane?
options: {'A': "It will continue running until the original pin's 12-beat expiration", 'B': 'It will run unpinned with the normal seven-tile capacity', 'C': 'It will no longer run because upgrades reset pins and underscore lanes are invisible unless pinned', 'D': 'It will be automatically renamed to `audit`'}
rationale: An upgrade resets all pins, and a leading-underscore lane never runs unless it is pinned.

stem: A configuration key documented as available only in Tessellate 4.3 is added to a system still running Tessellate 4.2. The system starts without errors, but the setting has no effect. What is the most likely explanation?
options: {'A': 'The setting will activate automatically after 12 beats', 'B': 'The running version does not recognize the key and silently ignores it', 'C': 'The setting applies only while a ferry is in transit', 'D': 'The setting was converted into a lane-level permission'}
rationale: Tessellate ignores configuration keys unknown to the running version without issuing a warning.

stem: A 3 MB ferry into lane R has `ferry.eager = true`. Lane R contains four tiles and runs for three beats. Which outcome should an operator expect?
options: {'A': 'The payloads arrive in order, and R accrues a billing weight of 12.', 'B': 'Each payload may have out-of-order shards, and R accrues a billing weight of 24.', 'C': 'Each payload may have out-of-order shards, and R accrues a billing weight of 12.', 'D': 'The payloads arrive in order, and R accrues a billing weight of 24.'}
rationale: A 3 MB ferry is sharded because it exceeds 2 MB, and Tessellate does not reorder shards. R's base weight is 4 tiles × 3 beats = 12; eager mode doubles the receiving lane's weight to 24.

stem: A lane receives 5 MB ordered event batches through a ferry. Checksums pass, but events are occasionally processed in the wrong order. What is the best diagnosis and fix?
options: {'A': 'The ferry is checked only every fifth beat; enable tracing to restore order.', 'B': 'The batches are sharded, and Tessellate may deliver shards out of order; include sequence numbers and reorder at the receiver.', 'C': 'The receiving lane has exceeded seven tiles; pinning it will restore ferry order.', 'D': 'The ledger was compacted, which removed ordering metadata; disable compaction.'}
rationale: Ferries larger than 2 MB are split into shards that may arrive out of order. Tessellate does not reorder them, so order-sensitive data must carry sequencing information.

stem: A tile first runs with input version V1 and fails. Its `retry.limit` is 6. Before its retries begin, upstream publishes corrected version V2. What will the tile's retries do?
options: {'A': 'They use V2 and follow normal retry back-off.', 'B': 'They use V2 and fire immediately without back-off.', 'C': 'They reuse V1 and follow normal retry back-off.', 'D': 'They reuse V1 and fire immediately without back-off.'}
rationale: Retries always reuse the original inputs, so they continue with V1. A retry limit above 5 disables back-off, causing the retries to fire immediately.

stem: A tile failed because its original upstream input was malformed. The upstream data is now corrected, but repeated retries still see the malformed value. Which action will make the work use the corrected input?
options: {'A': 'Increase `retry.limit` to 6.', 'B': 'Compact the ledger before the next retry.', 'C': 'Start a new tile invocation after the upstream correction instead of retrying the failed invocation.', 'D': "Pin the tile's lane before retrying."}
rationale: A retry is bound to the failed tile's original inputs. A new invocation is required to capture the corrected upstream data.

stem: The `_heartbeat` lane contains exactly three tiles and must run on every beat for 30 beats without any tile being queued. Which setup satisfies the requirement?
options: {'A': 'Leave it unpinned but rename it `_heartbeat_fast`.', 'B': 'Pin it once at deployment and make no further pin operations.', 'C': 'Pin it at deployment and issue `pin.renew` every 10 beats.', 'D': 'Pin it at deployment, add a fourth monitoring tile, and renew every 10 beats.'}
rationale: An underscore lane does not run unless pinned. Pinning guarantees execution every beat, caps the lane at three tiles, and expires after 12 beats unless renewed. Renewal every 10 beats keeps the pin active.

stem: An underscore lane was pinned and ran normally for exactly 12 beats. It then stopped running even though its tiles did not fail, no upgrade occurred, and its configuration was otherwise unchanged. What is the most likely cause?
options: {'A': 'The pin expired because `pin.renew` was not issued.', 'B': 'The lane became invisible after its twelfth beat despite still being pinned.', 'C': 'Pinned lanes automatically stop after accumulating three completed tiles.', 'D': 'The scheduler rejected the lane because underscore lanes cannot be pinned.'}
rationale: Pins expire after 12 beats unless renewed. Once the pin expires, an underscore lane is invisible to the scheduler and does not run.

stem: Two running lanes are each half-full, and their tiles can safely share one lane. Which change is guaranteed by Tessellate's cost rules to reduce future billing weight?
options: {'A': 'Run `ledger.compact` after every beat.', 'B': 'Merge the two half-full lanes into one lane.', 'C': 'Split each lane into two smaller lanes.', 'D': 'Retain both lanes but delete old ledger history manually.'}
rationale: Tessellate explicitly reduces billing weight when two half-full lanes are merged. Ledger compaction only reduces stored history, while splitting lanes never reduces billing weight.

stem: Which operator statement contains a mistaken assumption about Tessellate billing?
options: {'A': '“Compacting the ledger will lower billing weight because less history is stored.”', 'B': '“An idle tile still contributes to billing while its lane is running.”', 'C': '“Merging two half-full lanes can reduce billing weight.”', 'D': '“Splitting a lane does not reduce billing weight.”'}
rationale: `ledger.compact` reduces stored history but has no effect on billing weight. The other statements match Tessellate's billing rules.

stem: A lane already contains seven tiles. An operator submits an eighth tile to that lane. What happens?
options: {'A': 'The entire lane fails because it exceeded capacity.', 'B': 'The eighth tile is silently queued.', 'C': 'The eighth tile is automatically moved to a new lane.', 'D': 'The oldest tile is evicted to make room.'}
rationale: A lane holds at most seven tiles. An eighth tile is silently queued rather than rejected or moved.

stem: Eight tiles must all be admitted without queuing, and every tile must exchange results with every other tile. Using ordinary lane memory and ferries, which layout works?
options: {'A': 'Place all eight tiles in one lane so they can share memory directly.', 'B': 'Place four tiles in each of two lanes and rely on shared memory across the lanes.', 'C': 'Place four tiles in each of two lanes and configure a ferry in each direction between the lanes.', 'D': 'Place each tile in its own lane and use gates, without ferries, to expose the results.'}
rationale: One lane cannot admit all eight tiles because the eighth would be queued. Tiles share memory only within a lane, so two four-tile lanes require ferries in both directions for all tiles to exchange results.

stem: A gate is checked at the start of each 40-second beat. Its named condition becomes true one second after the check on beat 8. When can the blocked tile first pass the gate?
options: {'A': 'Immediately when the condition becomes true on beat 8', 'B': 'At the gate check on beat 9', 'C': 'At the metrics sample on beat 10', 'D': 'After the condition has remained true for 12 beats'}
rationale: Gates are checked once per beat, not continuously. Because the condition became true after beat 8's check, the tile must wait for beat 9's check.

stem: A tile had already passed a gate whose condition was supplied by data currently inside a ferry. An operator took a snapshot and later restored it. The tile is now blocked at the gate, and the condition data never appears. What best explains both symptoms?
options: {'A': 'Restoring resets retry inputs and disables the ferry for one beat', 'B': 'Snapshots omit lane memory, and restored pins expire immediately', 'C': 'Restoring re-runs gates from scratch, while snapshots do not capture ferry contents in transit', 'D': 'Gate state is restored, but ferry shards are always discarded after 12 beats'}
rationale: A restore re-runs gates from scratch, so a tile that had passed can block again. The snapshot contains lane memory but not the condition data that was still in the ferry.

stem: One tile must read every lane, including `_audit`, but the other tiles currently sharing its lane must retain narrower access. Which design satisfies the requirement with the least access?
options: {'A': 'Grant `wide` to the individual tile while leaving it in the shared lane', 'B': 'Move the tile to a dedicated lane and grant that lane `wide`', 'C': 'Grant `wide` to the shared lane and revoke it from each neighboring tile', 'D': 'Pin the shared lane and grant `wide` only during beats when the tile runs'}
rationale: The `wide` scope permits access to every lane, including underscore lanes, but permissions are inherited from the lane. A dedicated `wide` lane prevents unrelated tiles from inheriting that access.

stem: An operator grants `wide` to a lane so one reporting tile can read `_audit`. Why is this grant over-broad if the lane also contains six unrelated tiles?
options: {'A': 'It causes every tile in every lane to read `_audit`', 'B': 'It doubles the billing weight of all seven tiles', 'C': 'All tiles in that lane inherit `wide` and can read every lane', 'D': 'It automatically pins the lane and reduces its capacity'}
rationale: Permissions are inherited from the lane, so all seven tiles receive `wide`, which allows them to read every lane, including underscore lanes.

stem: At snapshot time, lane `L` contains `state=v4`, a ferry carrying `delta=v5` is in transit to `L`, and a tile in `L` has already passed gate `ready`. What should be expected after restoring that snapshot?
options: {'A': '`state=v4` is restored, `delta=v5` is not restored, and the tile must evaluate gate `ready` again', 'B': '`state=v4` and `delta=v5` are restored, and the tile remains past the gate', 'C': 'Only `delta=v5` is restored, and the gate remains passed', 'D': 'Neither value is restored, but the tile remains past the gate'}
rationale: Snapshots capture lane memory, so `state=v4` returns. They do not capture in-transit ferry contents, and restores re-run gates from scratch.

stem: A producer sent its only copy of a result through a ferry. A snapshot was taken after the result left the producer but before it reached the receiving lane. After restoring, the result is missing from both lanes. What is the most likely cause?
options: {'A': 'Snapshots retain only tile outputs, not lane memory', 'B': 'The result was in ferry transit, which snapshots do not capture', 'C': 'Restoring automatically compacts ferry data out of the ledger', 'D': 'Ferries discard all data whenever a gate is restored'}
rationale: Snapshots capture lane memory but not ferry contents in transit. At snapshot time, the result was no longer in the producer's memory and had not yet entered the receiver's memory.

stem: A tile emits a suspect value and then fails validation. Enabling `trace` on that tile does not record the value. Which approach can capture the value using Tessellate's tracing behavior?
options: {'A': 'Enable `trace` twice so the second trace records outputs', 'B': 'Wait for a fifth-beat metrics sample, which includes tile outputs', 'C': 'Send the value to a diagnostic tile as an input and enable `trace` on that diagnostic tile', 'D': 'Pin the failing tile so `trace` switches from inputs to outputs'}
rationale: The `trace` flag records inputs only. Making the suspect value an input to a diagnostic tile allows that tile's trace to record it.

stem: A counter briefly changed from 0 to 1 on beat 12 and returned to 0 on beat 13. Metrics show 0 on beats 10 and 15 and contain no record of the change. Tracing was not enabled. Why is the change absent?
options: {'A': 'Metrics record only outputs from pinned lanes', 'B': 'Metrics are sampled every fifth beat, so the event occurred entirely between samples', 'C': 'Metrics discard values that persist for fewer than three retries', 'D': 'Metrics are stored only when a ferry crosses a lane boundary'}
rationale: Metrics are sampled only on every fifth beat. The change occurred after the beat-10 sample and ended before the beat-15 sample, so it was never recorded.

stem: Before an upgrade, pinned underscore lane `_audit` runs every beat. Immediately after upgrading Tessellate, no configuration is reapplied. What should the operator expect?
options: {'A': '`_audit` continues running until its original pin reaches 12 beats', 'B': '`_audit` runs but is restored to the normal seven-tile capacity', 'C': 'The upgrade resets the pin, so `_audit` will not run until it is pinned again', 'D': 'The upgrade renames `_audit` to make it scheduler-visible'}
rationale: Upgrading Tessellate resets all pins. Because underscore lanes are invisible to the scheduler and never run unless pinned, `_audit` stops running until repinned.

stem: An operator deploys configuration containing `gate.poll_interval=5s`, a key introduced only in Tessellate 5, but the server is still running Tessellate 4. The deployment reports no error, and gates continue to be checked once per beat. What is the best diagnosis?
options: {'A': 'The key is queued until the next pin renewal', 'B': 'The running version ignores unknown configuration keys without warning', 'C': 'Five-second gate polling applies only to underscore lanes', 'D': 'The key took effect, but metrics conceal the extra gate checks'}
rationale: Tessellate silently ignores configuration keys unknown to the running version, so the Tessellate 5 key has no effect on Tessellate 4.

stem: A 3 MB ferry sends data to a receiving lane containing four tiles. The lane runs for three beats, and ferry.eager is set to true. What outcome should the operator expect?
options: {'A': 'The receiving lane has a billing weight of 24, and the ferry shards may arrive out of order.', 'B': 'The receiving lane has a billing weight of 24, and Tessellate reorders the ferry shards automatically.', 'C': 'The receiving lane has a billing weight of 12, and the ferry shards may arrive out of order.', 'D': 'The ferry is rejected because it is larger than 2 MB, and the receiving lane has a billing weight of 12.'}
rationale: Four tiles over three beats have weight 12, eager mode doubles that to 24, and a ferry larger than 2 MB is sharded without automatic reordering.

stem: A 3.5 MB ordered record stream is sent through a ferry, but the receiving lane sometimes processes later records before earlier records. What is the most likely cause?
options: {'A': 'The ferry is split into shards larger than 2 MB, and Tessellate may deliver those shards out of order.', 'B': 'The receiving lane has more than three tiles, so Tessellate randomly reorders its memory.', 'C': 'Ferries copy data continuously, allowing records to overtake one another between beats.', 'D': 'The trace flag records inputs instead of outputs, which changes the delivery order.'}
rationale: Ferries larger than 2 MB are split into shards that may arrive out of order because Tessellate does not reorder them.

stem: A tile starts with input version 1 and fails. Its retry.limit is set to 6, and upstream changes the data to version 2 before the retries begin. How will the tile retry?
options: {'A': 'It will make six retries immediately, and every retry will use input version 1.', 'B': 'It will make six retries with back-off, and every retry will use input version 2.', 'C': 'It will make three retries immediately, alternating between input versions 1 and 2.', 'D': 'It will make no retries because retry limits above 5 disable retries entirely.'}
rationale: A retry limit above 5 disables back-off, while all retries continue to use the tile's original inputs.

stem: A tile failed using an outdated upstream value, and its automatic retries keep using that same value even though upstream has produced a correction. What should the operator do to process the corrected value?
options: {'A': 'Stop relying on the existing retries and start a new tile execution after the corrected upstream value is available.', 'B': 'Raise retry.limit above 5 so the next retry refreshes its inputs.', 'C': 'Run ledger.compact before allowing another retry.', 'D': 'Pin the lane so its retries read the newest upstream value.'}
rationale: Retries always reuse the original inputs, so processing the corrected value requires a new tile execution rather than another retry.

stem: The underscore lane _audit contains three tiles and must run on every beat for 30 beats. Which setup meets the requirement?
options: {'A': 'Pin _audit and renew its pin before each 12-beat expiration.', 'B': 'Pin _audit once, because a pin lasts for the entire run.', 'C': 'Add a fourth tile to _audit and pin it to prevent expiration.', 'D': 'Leave _audit unpinned and set retry.limit to 30.'}
rationale: An underscore lane must be pinned to run, a pinned lane can contain at most three tiles, and its pin must be renewed because pins expire after 12 beats.

stem: A pinned lane ran on every beat at first but stopped after 12 beats; no upgrade occurred, and the lane's tiles did not fail. What is the most likely explanation?
options: {'A': 'The pin expired because it was not renewed with pin.renew.', 'B': 'The lane reached the normal seven-tile capacity.', 'C': 'The scheduler automatically made the lane invisible after 12 beats.', 'D': 'The ledger stopped the lane to reduce billing weight.'}
rationale: Pins expire after 12 beats unless they are renewed with pin.renew.

stem: Two normal lanes each contain three tiles and perform the same workflow for the same number of beats. Which change reduces billing weight under Tessellate's ledger rules while preserving the six tiles?
options: {'A': 'Merge the two half-full lanes into one six-tile lane.', 'B': 'Split each lane into three one-tile lanes.', 'C': 'Keep the lanes unchanged and run ledger.compact after every beat.', 'D': 'Connect both lanes to eager ferries.'}
rationale: Tessellate specifies that merging two half-full lanes reduces billing weight, whereas splitting does not and ledger compaction only reduces stored history.

stem: Which operator statement contains a mistaken assumption about Tessellate billing?
options: {'A': 'Idle tiles still count when their lane is running.', 'B': "Running ledger.compact will lower the workflow's billing weight.", 'C': 'An eager ferry doubles the billing weight of every tile in its receiving lane.', 'D': 'Splitting a lane does not reduce billing weight.'}
rationale: The ledger.compact command reduces stored history but does not reduce billing weight.

stem: A normal lane already contains seven tiles, and an operator submits an eighth tile to that lane. What happens?
options: {'A': 'The eighth tile is silently queued.', 'B': 'The eighth tile is rejected with a capacity error.', 'C': 'The oldest tile is moved automatically to another lane.', 'D': 'The lane is automatically pinned and reduced to three tiles.'}
rationale: A normal lane holds at most seven tiles, and an eighth tile is silently queued rather than rejected.

stem: Eight tiles must all be admitted without capacity queuing, and tiles in either group must be able to exchange data with the other group. Which layout meets these requirements?
options: {'A': 'Place all eight tiles in one normal lane.', 'B': 'Place four tiles in each of two normal lanes and connect the lanes with a ferry.', 'C': 'Place four tiles in each of two normal lanes without a ferry.', 'D': 'Place all eight tiles in one pinned lane.'}
rationale: Two four-tile lanes avoid the seven-tile lane limit, and a ferry is required for data exchange between different lanes.

stem: A gate is checked at time 0 and is false. Its condition becomes true at time 10 seconds and remains true. With the default 40-second beat, when can the blocked tile proceed?
options: {'A': 'Immediately at 10 seconds', 'B': 'At 20 seconds', 'C': 'At 40 seconds', 'D': 'At 50 seconds'}
rationale: Gates are checked only once per beat, so the condition is not recognized until the next check at 40 seconds.

stem: A tile passed a gate while the condition was true, and a snapshot was then taken. Later the condition became false. After the snapshot is restored, the tile is blocked at the same gate again. What best explains this behavior?
options: {'A': "Restoring a snapshot changes the gate's name", 'B': 'A restore reruns gates from scratch, so the false condition blocks the tile again', 'C': 'Snapshots preserve ferry contents but discard gate definitions', 'D': 'Gates are permanently closed after a snapshot is restored'}
rationale: Restoring a snapshot reruns gates from scratch, so even a previously passed gate can block when its condition is now false.

stem: One tile must read an underscore lane, but no other tile should receive that access. Which configuration provides the least access permitted by Tessellate 4?
options: {'A': 'Move the tile into a lane by itself and grant that lane the wide scope', 'B': 'Keep the tile in its current shared lane and grant only the tile the wide scope', 'C': 'Grant the current shared lane the wide scope and give its other tiles narrower scopes', 'D': 'Keep the lane narrow and pin the tile so it can read the underscore lane'}
rationale: Reading an underscore lane requires wide scope, and isolating the tile is necessary because permissions are inherited from the lane rather than assigned more narrowly to individual tiles.

stem: A lane contains four tiles, but only one of them needs to read another lane. An operator grants the entire lane the wide scope. What is the resulting over-broad access?
options: {'A': 'Only the requesting tile can read the other lane', 'B': 'All four tiles can read every lane, including underscore lanes', 'C': 'All four tiles can read only non-underscore lanes', 'D': 'The requesting tile can read every lane, while the other tiles lose access to their own lane'}
rationale: Scope is inherited from the lane, and wide scope permits every tile in that lane to read every lane, including underscore lanes.

stem: A snapshot is taken after a tile has passed a gate, while a ferry shard is still in transit between lanes. What happens when that snapshot is later restored?
options: {'A': 'Lane memory and the in-transit shard are restored, and the gate remains passed', 'B': 'Lane memory is restored, the in-transit shard is not restored, and the gate is evaluated again', 'C': 'Only the in-transit shard is restored, and lane memory is cleared', 'D': 'Lane memory is restored, the shard is reordered automatically, and all gates are removed'}
rationale: Snapshots capture lane memory but not ferry contents in transit, and restoring them reruns gates from scratch.

stem: A payload had left its source lane in a ferry but had not reached the destination when a snapshot was taken. After restoring that snapshot, the destination never sees the payload. What is the most likely cause?
options: {'A': 'Snapshots exclude ferry contents that are in transit', 'B': 'Snapshots erase all destination-lane memory', 'C': 'Ferries stop permanently after any restore', 'D': 'Restores reject payloads smaller than 2 MB'}
rationale: The payload was lost because snapshots do not capture ferry contents that are still in transit.

stem: An operator enables trace to investigate a tile whose produced value causes a failure, but the value does not appear in the trace. What should the operator do to capture it?
options: {'A': 'Increase the retry limit so trace begins recording outputs', 'B': "Add explicit instrumentation that records the tile's output before the failure", 'C': 'Compact the ledger to reveal the output in trace history', 'D': 'Pin the lane so trace switches from inputs to outputs'}
rationale: The trace flag records only tile inputs, so output capture requires separate explicit instrumentation.

stem: A short-lived error condition begins just after the metric sample on beat 10 and clears before beat 15. The system remains healthy, but no metric records the condition. Why?
options: {'A': 'Metrics are recorded only for pinned lanes', 'B': 'Metrics are sampled only on every fifth beat, so the condition occurred entirely between samples', 'C': 'Metrics omit errors whenever retry back-off is enabled', 'D': 'Metric history is stored only after ledger compaction'}
rationale: Tessellate samples metrics every fifth beat and does not record events that begin and end between those samples.

stem: An underscore lane named `_audit` is pinned and running before a Tessellate upgrade. Its configuration is otherwise unchanged. What should the operator expect immediately after the upgrade?
options: {'A': 'The lane keeps running because upgrades extend existing pins', 'B': 'The lane stops running until it is pinned again', 'C': 'The lane becomes visible to the scheduler because its pin was reset', 'D': 'The lane runs unpinned for 12 beats and then stops'}
rationale: An upgrade resets all pins, and an underscore lane never runs unless it is pinned.

stem: An operator adds a configuration key documented only for a newer Tessellate version. On the current older version, startup succeeds without a warning, but the setting has no effect. What is the best diagnosis?
options: {'A': 'The key is queued until the next fifth beat', 'B': 'The key is unknown to the running version and was silently ignored', 'C': 'The key cannot take effect until the ledger is compacted', 'D': 'The key was converted into a lane-level permission'}
rationale: Configuration keys unknown to the running Tessellate version are ignored without warning.

stem: A 3 MB ferry sends data into lane B, which has four tiles and runs for three beats. `ferry.eager = true`, and no other lanes contribute to the bill. Which result should the operator expect?
options: {'A': 'Billing weight 12; shards are reassembled in source order.', 'B': 'Billing weight 24; shards are reassembled in source order.', 'C': 'Billing weight 24; shards may arrive in a different order.', 'D': 'Billing weight 12; shards may arrive in a different order.'}
rationale: The payload exceeds 2 MB, so it is sharded without automatic reordering. Lane B normally contributes 4 × 3 = 12 billing weight, which eager ferry delivery doubles to 24.

stem: A source lane emits a correctly ordered 3.5 MB batch. After the batch crosses a ferry, a receiving tile observes later records before earlier records. No tile modifies the batch. What explains the changed sequence?
options: {'A': 'The beat boundary sorts ferry records by their arrival timestamps.', 'B': 'The payload is sharded, and Tessellate does not resequence the shards.', 'C': 'The receiving lane shares memory with the source during transfer.', 'D': 'The lane scheduler swaps records when a tile waits for capacity.'}
rationale: Ferries split payloads larger than 2 MB into shards, which may arrive out of order and are not reordered by Tessellate.

stem: A tile has `retry.limit = 6` and originally receives input version v1. The upstream value changes to v2 before the tile's first retry. What retry behavior should the operator expect?
options: {'A': 'Six retries with back-off, all using v2.', 'B': 'Six immediate retries, all using v2.', 'C': 'Six retries with back-off, all using v1.', 'D': 'Six immediate retries, all using v1.'}
rationale: A retry limit above five disables back-off, while every retry continues to use the tile's original inputs.

stem: A tile failed with input version v1. The upstream lane now contains v2, but each automatic retry continues processing v1. Which change makes the next processing attempt use v2?
options: {'A': 'Start a new tile execution after v2 is available.', 'B': 'Increase `retry.limit` after v2 is available.', 'C': "Pin the tile's lane after v2 is available.", 'D': 'Enable eager ferry delivery after v2 is available.'}
rationale: Retries reuse the original inputs, so changing retry or scheduling settings will not refresh them. A new tile execution can take the updated input.

stem: The underscore lane `_settle` contains three tiles and must run on every beat for a 20-beat job. Which setup meets that requirement?
options: {'A': 'Pin the lane at launch and let that pin cover all 20 beats.', 'B': 'Leave the lane unpinned and schedule it with a recurring gate.', 'C': 'Pin the lane at launch and issue `pin.renew` on beat 12.', 'D': 'Pin each tile separately and renew the tiles after beat 12.'}
rationale: An underscore lane must be pinned to run, and a pin guarantees execution every beat. Because pins expire after 12 beats, the lane pin must be renewed.

stem: A two-tile lane named `payments` was pinned at the start of a run. With no upgrade or `pin.renew`, it ran for 12 beats and then stopped being scheduled. What is the most likely cause?
options: {'A': 'The scheduler queued the lane after its twelfth execution.', 'B': "The lane's pin expired because it was not renewed.", 'C': 'The three-tile pinning cap changed to a two-tile cap.', 'D': 'The metrics sampling interval suspended later executions.'}
rationale: Pins expire after 12 beats unless renewed with `pin.renew`, so the lane no longer has its guaranteed schedule.

stem: Two lanes each contain three tiles, run for the same beats, and have no eager ferry configured. Which change reduces their billing weight while retaining all six tiles?
options: {'A': 'Split the two lanes into six separate one-tile lanes.', 'B': 'Run `ledger.compact` after their final scheduled beat.', 'C': 'Move one tile between the lanes while keeping both active.', 'D': 'Merge the two lanes into a single six-tile lane.'}
rationale: Tessellate's billing rules state that merging two half-full lanes reduces billing weight. Splitting does not, compaction affects history rather than billing, and redistribution leaves both lanes active.

stem: An operator runs `ledger.compact` nightly and expects the monthly billing weight to fall even though tile execution is unchanged. Which assessment is correct?
options: {'A': 'History storage shrinks, but billing weight stays unchanged.', 'B': 'Past beat charges shrink, but future charges stay unchanged.', 'C': 'Idle-tile charges shrink, but active-tile charges stay unchanged.', 'D': 'Ferry charges shrink, but lane charges stay unchanged.'}
rationale: `ledger.compact` reduces stored history but has no effect on billing weight.

stem: A lane already contains seven tiles when an operator submits an eighth tile to that lane. What does Tessellate do with the new tile?
options: {'A': 'It starts the tile as a temporary eighth occupant.', 'B': 'It rejects the tile and records a capacity failure.', 'C': 'It accepts the tile but silently places it in a queue.', 'D': 'It places the tile in an automatically created lane.'}
rationale: A lane holds at most seven tiles; an eighth tile is silently queued rather than rejected.

stem: Eight tiles must run without any tile waiting for lane capacity, and they need to pass changing data between the groups during the run. Which layout meets both requirements?
options: {'A': 'Place all eight tiles in one lane and use shared memory.', 'B': 'Place four tiles in each of two lanes and connect them by ferry.', 'C': 'Place four tiles in each of two lanes and connect them by gate.', 'D': 'Place four tiles in each of two lanes and restore shared snapshots.'}
rationale: Eight tiles cannot run together in one seven-tile lane. Separate lanes require a ferry to exchange data, so a four-and-four split connected by ferry satisfies both requirements.

stem: Gate checks occur at beat boundaries of 0, 40, and 80 seconds. A tile's condition is false at 40 seconds and becomes true at 55 seconds. When can the tile begin running?
options: {'A': 'At 55 seconds', 'B': 'At 60 seconds', 'C': 'At 80 seconds', 'D': 'At 95 seconds'}
rationale: Gates are evaluated once per beat, so the condition is not detected until the 80-second boundary.

stem: A snapshot was taken after a tile had passed a gate. When the snapshot is restored later, the named condition is false and the tile is blocked again. What explains the change in status?
options: {'A': 'The snapshot omitted the condition because it was in a ferry.', 'B': 'The restore reevaluated the gate against the current condition.', 'C': 'A retry returned the tile to the previously passed gate.', 'D': 'An expired pin suspended the lane before the gate check.'}
rationale: Restoring a snapshot reruns gates from scratch, so a tile that had previously passed can block if the condition is now false.

stem: A reconciliation tile in the `reports` lane needs to read `reports` and `billing`, but no other lanes. Other tiles in `reports` must retain their existing broad access. Which change meets the reconciliation tile's least-access requirement?
options: {'A': 'Keep the lane wide and assign the tile a narrower scope.', 'B': "Keep the lane wide and gate the tile's cross-lane reads.", 'C': "Remove wide from the lane and narrow every tile's scope.", 'D': 'Move the tile to a lane scoped for reports and billing.'}
rationale: Permissions are inherited from the lane, so a tile cannot be narrower than its current lane. Moving it to an appropriately scoped lane provides the required access without changing the other tiles.

stem: The `ops` lane has the `wide` scope because its scanner reads `_audit`. An exporter in the same lane is intended to read only `ops`. Which security finding is accurate?
options: {'A': 'The `wide` scope also reaches the exporter through lane inheritance.', 'B': 'The `wide` scope reaches the exporter after its first successful run.', 'C': 'The `wide` scope reaches the exporter while the scanner is active.', 'D': 'The `wide` scope reaches the exporter when a ferry is attached.'}
rationale: Every tile inherits its lane's permissions, so the exporter receives broad access even though it does not require it.

stem: At beat 10, a snapshot is taken while lane memory contains `quota=20` and a ferry shard is in transit. Later, memory changes to `quota=35` and the shard is delivered. What state results from restoring the beat-10 snapshot?
options: {'A': 'Memory has `quota=35`, and the shard is reinstated.', 'B': 'Memory has `quota=35`, and the shard is not reinstated.', 'C': 'Memory has `quota=20`, and the shard is not reinstated.', 'D': 'Memory has `quota=20`, and the shard is reinstated.'}
rationale: The restore recovers lane memory from the snapshot but does not recover ferry contents that were in transit.

stem: A producer sent a record through a ferry, and a snapshot was taken before the record reached the receiving lane. After a later restore, the record is absent from both lanes. What is the most likely cause?
options: {'A': 'The payload was omitted because it had not reached lane memory.', 'B': 'The payload was discarded because its shards arrived out of order.', 'C': 'The payload was rolled back because the receiving lane was unpinned.', 'D': 'The payload was removed because ledger history was compacted.'}
rationale: Snapshots capture lane memory but exclude ferry contents in transit, so the record was not part of the saved state.

stem: A producer passes a malformed value to a validator, which then fails. The team wants the `trace` flag to record the value passed by the producer. Which tracing arrangement will capture it?
options: {'A': "Trace the producer and inspect the producer's recorded output.", 'B': "Trace the validator and inspect the validator's recorded input.", 'C': "Trace the producer and inspect the validator's recorded output.", 'D': "Trace the validator and inspect the producer's recorded input."}
rationale: Trace records a tile's inputs rather than its outputs. The producer's value becomes an input to the validator.

stem: Metrics are normal at beats 5 and 10, but an event log reports a brief resource spike during beat 7. Why is there no metric point showing the spike?
options: {'A': 'Beat 7 fell between the scheduled metric samples.', 'B': 'Beat 7 was averaged into the metric for beat 10.', 'C': 'Beat 7 was suppressed while the affected tile retried.', 'D': 'Beat 7 was deferred until the affected lane filled.'}
rationale: Metrics are sampled on every fifth beat, and events between those samples are not recorded.

stem: The pinned underscore lane `_audit` is running before a Tessellate upgrade. No configuration is changed after the upgrade. What should an operator expect on the next beat?
options: {'A': 'It runs under its prior pin until the original expiration.', 'B': 'It runs under a renewed pin created during the upgrade.', 'C': 'It queues excess tiles while retaining the prior pin.', 'D': 'It pauses because the upgrade removed the prior pin.'}
rationale: An upgrade resets all pins. Because underscore lanes do not run unless pinned, `_audit` pauses until it is pinned again.

stem: A configuration entry changes behavior in a Tessellate 4.4 staging environment. The same file is loaded by a 4.2 production environment, which starts cleanly but shows no behavioral change or warning. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: {'A': 'Version 4.2 does not recognize the entry and silently ignores it.', 'B': 'Version 4.2 defers the entry until the next metric sample.', 'C': 'Version 4.2 stores the entry until its ledger is compacted.', 'D': 'Version 4.2 applies the entry after the current pin expires.'}
rationale: A running Tessellate version ignores unknown configuration keys without issuing a warning.

stem: A 3 MB ferry sends data to a receiving lane containing four tiles. The ferry has eager mode enabled, and the receiving lane runs for two beats. Which outcome should the operator expect?
options: {'A': 'The ferry transfers once per beat, its shards may arrive out of order, and the receiving lane accrues a billing weight of 16.', 'B': 'The ferry transfers continuously, its shards are reordered automatically, and the receiving lane accrues a billing weight of 8.', 'C': 'The ferry transfers once per beat, its shards may arrive out of order, and the receiving lane accrues a billing weight of 8.', 'D': 'The ferry transfers only on the first beat, its shards are reordered automatically, and the receiving lane accrues a billing weight of 16.'}
rationale: A payload over 2 MB is sharded without reordering, ferries copy once per beat, and eager mode doubles the lane's normal weight of four tiles times two beats from 8 to 16.

stem: A producer sends a 2.8 MB ordered record stream through a ferry, but the consumer sometimes sees later records before earlier records even though the producer emitted them correctly. What is the most likely cause?
options: {'A': 'Ferries transfer only every fifth beat, causing records from different samples to mix.', 'B': 'The payload is split into shards, and Tessellate does not reorder shards that arrive out of order.', 'C': 'The receiving lane shares memory with the producer lane, allowing records to bypass the ferry.', 'D': 'Eager mode reverses record order while reducing latency.'}
rationale: Ferries larger than 2 MB are sharded, and Tessellate permits those shards to arrive out of order without reordering them.

stem: A tile has retry limit set to 6. It fails, and its upstream data changes immediately afterward. Assuming retries occur, which behavior should the operator expect?
options: {'A': 'The retries use the changed upstream data and apply progressively longer back-off delays.', 'B': "The retries use the tile's original inputs and fire immediately without back-off.", 'C': 'The retries use the changed upstream data and fire immediately without back-off.', 'D': "The retries use the tile's original inputs but remain spaced by the default back-off."}
rationale: Retries always reuse the original inputs, and setting retry limit above 5 disables retry back-off entirely.

stem: A tile failed after reading an outdated upstream value, and the upstream value has now been corrected. The next attempt must consume the corrected value. What should the operator do?
options: {'A': 'Increase retry limit so the next retry refreshes its inputs.', 'B': 'Enable eager mode on the upstream ferry so the pending retry replaces its original inputs.', 'C': "Start a new tile execution whose original inputs include the corrected value instead of relying on the failed tile's retry.", 'D': 'Run ledger compact before the retry so cached tile inputs are removed.'}
rationale: Because retries always reuse the failed tile's original inputs, a new tile execution is required to take the corrected upstream value as an original input.

stem: Four independent tiles in underscore-prefixed lanes must each be guaranteed to run on every beat for 30 beats. The tiles may be divided between lanes. Which setup satisfies the requirement?
options: {'A': 'Place all four tiles in one underscore lane, pin it, and renew the pin before every 12-beat expiration.', 'B': 'Split the tiles between two underscore lanes with no more than three tiles in either lane, pin both lanes, and renew both pins before each 12-beat expiration.', 'C': 'Split the tiles between two underscore lanes, pin both once at the start, and rely on the pins for all 30 beats.', 'D': 'Remove the leading underscores, put all four tiles in one unpinned lane, and rely on scheduler visibility to guarantee execution every beat.'}
rationale: Underscore lanes must be pinned, a pinned lane can contain at most three tiles, and each pin must be renewed because it expires after 12 beats.

stem: An underscore-prefixed lane ran on every beat after being pinned, then stopped running after 12 beats; no upgrade occurred and the lane configuration did not change. What is the most likely diagnosis and fix?
options: {'A': 'The lane reached the normal seven-tile limit, so split it into two unpinned lanes.', 'B': 'Its pin expired, so renew it with pin.renew.', 'C': 'The scheduler hid the lane despite an active pin, so grant its tiles wide scope.', 'D': 'Its retry back-off disabled scheduling, so reduce retry limit to 5.'}
rationale: Pins expire after 12 beats unless renewed with pin.renew, and an underscore lane does not run without a pin.

stem: Two lanes each contain three tiles. Which change does Tessellate explicitly define as reducing billing weight, assuming the six tiles can fit in one lane?
options: {'A': 'Merge the two half-full lanes into one six-tile lane.', 'B': 'Split each lane into three one-tile lanes.', 'C': 'Run ledger.compact after every beat.', 'D': 'Enable eager mode on a ferry whose receiving lane contains the tiles.'}
rationale: Tessellate explicitly states that merging two half-full lanes reduces billing weight, while splitting never does, ledger compaction does not, and eager mode doubles receiving-lane weight.

stem: Which operator statement is based on a mistaken assumption about Tessellate billing?
options: {'A': 'Running ledger.compact will reduce our billing weight because it removes stored history.', 'B': 'Idle tiles still add billing weight when their lane is running.', 'C': 'Enabling eager mode doubles the billing weight of every tile in the receiving lane.', 'D': 'Splitting a lane does not reduce billing weight.'}
rationale: Ledger compaction reduces stored history but has no effect on billing weight.

stem: A lane already contains seven tiles, and an operator submits an eighth tile to that lane. What happens?
options: {'A': 'The eighth tile is rejected with a capacity error.', 'B': 'The oldest tile is evicted and replaced by the eighth tile.', 'C': 'The eighth tile is silently queued rather than rejected.', 'D': 'The lane automatically splits into two lanes.'}
rationale: A lane holds at most seven tiles, and an eighth tile is silently queued.

stem: Eight tiles must be active at the same time, and tiles placed in different lanes must exchange working data. Which layout is valid?
options: {'A': 'Place all eight tiles in one lane so they can share memory directly.', 'B': 'Divide the tiles between two lanes with at most seven tiles per lane and connect the lanes with a ferry.', 'C': 'Divide the tiles between two lanes and grant every tile wide scope, eliminating the need for a ferry.', 'D': 'Place seven tiles in one lane and submit the eighth to the same lane, where it will run concurrently from the queue.'}
rationale: Eight concurrently active tiles cannot fit in one seven-tile lane, and data between separate lanes must pass through a ferry.

stem: At the start of beat 21, a gate checks its named condition and finds it false. The condition becomes true three seconds later, and the beat duration is 40 seconds. When can the blocked tile run at the earliest?
options: {'A': 'Immediately when the condition becomes true', 'B': 'At the start of beat 22', 'C': 'At the start of beat 25, when metrics are sampled', 'D': 'After the condition has remained true for a full beat'}
rationale: Tessellate checks gates only once per beat, so a condition that changes after the beat 21 check cannot release the tile until beat 22.

stem: A tile passed a gate while the condition named approval was true, and an operator then took a snapshot. Later, approval became false and the operator restored that snapshot. The lane memory was restored correctly, but the tile is blocked at the gate again. What is the correct diagnosis?
options: {'A': 'Restoring a snapshot reruns gates from scratch, so the tile must wait for approval to become true again', 'B': 'The tile exhausted its three default retries before the snapshot was taken', 'C': 'Gate state is carried inside ferries, which snapshots do not capture', 'D': 'The lane lost its scheduling visibility because all restores remove pins'}
rationale: Snapshot restoration reruns gates from scratch even for tiles that had already passed them.

stem: One tile must read every lane, including an underscore lane, but no other tile in its current lane may receive that access. Which design satisfies the requirement with the least access?
options: {'A': 'Give only that tile the wide scope while leaving it in its current lane', 'B': 'Give its current lane the wide scope and declare narrower scopes on the other tiles', 'C': 'Move the tile to a dedicated lane and give that dedicated lane the wide scope', 'D': "Pin the tile's current lane and grant the tile access only to the underscore lane"}
rationale: Wide access is needed to read every lane, and isolating the tile in its own lane prevents lane-inherited permissions from widening access for its former lane mates.

stem: A lane has the wide scope because one of its tiles must inspect all other lanes. Another tile in that lane is configured with a narrow scope and is assumed to be unable to read an underscore lane. What is wrong with this assumption?
options: {'A': 'The narrow tile can read the underscore lane because permissions are inherited from the lane', 'B': 'The narrow tile can read the underscore lane only while the lane is pinned', 'C': 'The narrow tile cannot read any other lane unless a ferry is eager', 'D': 'The narrow tile receives wide access only after twelve beats'}
rationale: A tile cannot hold a narrower scope than its lane, so every tile in a wide-scoped lane has the lane's broad access.

stem: A snapshot is taken after a tile has passed a gate. At that moment, lane B's memory contains version 6, while a ferry shard carrying version 7 to lane B is still in transit. The snapshot is later restored when the gate's named condition is false. Which result should the operator expect?
options: {'A': 'Lane B contains version 7, and the tile remains past the gate', 'B': 'Lane B contains version 6, the in-transit shard is absent, and the tile blocks when the gate is rerun', 'C': 'Lane B contains version 6, the in-transit shard resumes delivery, and the tile remains past the gate', 'D': 'Lane B has no restored memory because snapshots capture only ferry contents'}
rationale: Snapshots restore lane memory but exclude in-transit ferry contents, and restoration causes gates to run again from scratch.

stem: Lane A sent data to lane B through a ferry, and a snapshot was taken while the data was in transit. After restoring the snapshot, lane A still has its original memory, but lane B never receives that ferry data. What best explains the loss?
options: {'A': 'Snapshots omit ferry contents that are in transit', 'B': 'Restores discard the memory of the sending lane', 'C': 'Ferries can deliver data only to pinned lanes after a restore', 'D': "The default retry process replaced the ferry data with the tile's original inputs"}
rationale: A Tessellate snapshot captures lane memory but does not capture data currently in a ferry.

stem: A Transform tile produces a suspect value, and the downstream Consumer tile fails while processing that value. Which action captures the suspect value using Tessellate's trace behavior?
options: {'A': "Enable trace on Transform, because trace records each tile's outputs", 'B': "Enable trace on Consumer, because the suspect output is one of Consumer's inputs", 'C': 'Enable metrics on Transform, because metrics retain every value between samples', 'D': 'Compact the ledger after the failure so the output is preserved in billing history'}
rationale: Trace records tile inputs but never outputs, so tracing Consumer captures the value that Transform supplied to it.

stem: A lane's error metric rises during beat 22 and returns to normal before beat 25. The metric is normal in the records from beats 20 and 25, and no error spike appears anywhere. The tiles continued running throughout. What is the most likely explanation?
options: {'A': 'Metrics are sampled only on every fifth beat, so the event occurred entirely between samples', 'B': 'Idle tiles overwrite error metrics whenever their lane remains running', 'C': 'Metrics from unpinned lanes are deleted after three beats', 'D': 'The trace flag suppresses output metrics when it records tile inputs'}
rationale: Tessellate samples metrics only on every fifth beat and does not record events that occur entirely between samples.

stem: An underscore lane is pinned and running before a Tessellate version upgrade. No pin is reapplied after the upgrade. What should the operator expect?
options: {'A': 'The lane continues running until the original pin reaches its twelfth beat', 'B': 'The lane becomes unpinned and does not run because underscore lanes are invisible to the scheduler', 'C': 'The lane remains pinned but its capacity increases from three tiles to seven', 'D': 'The lane runs once per fifth beat because upgrades convert pins into metric schedules'}
rationale: An upgrade resets all pins, and an unpinned underscore lane is invisible to the scheduler and never runs.

stem: A cluster is still running Tessellate 4.1, but its configuration includes a pin.renew key introduced in Tessellate 4.2. Configuration validation reports no error, yet the lane's pin expires after twelve beats. What is the correct diagnosis?
options: {'A': 'The running version does not recognize the key and ignores it without warning', 'B': 'Pin renewal is disabled whenever a lane contains more than three tiles', 'C': 'The key was accepted, but ledger compaction removed the renewed pin', 'D': 'Pin renewal works only for underscore lanes'}
rationale: Tessellate silently ignores configuration keys that are unknown to the version currently running.

stem: A 3 MB ferry sends data from lane Alpha to lane Beta with ferry.eager set to true. Beta contains four tiles and runs for five beats. Which outcome should the operator expect?
options: {'A': 'The payload remains whole, and only the tile that reads it has doubled billing weight.', 'B': 'The payload is sharded and may arrive out of order without reordering, while Beta contributes 40 units of billing weight.', 'C': 'The payload is sharded and automatically reordered, while Beta contributes 20 units of billing weight.', 'D': 'The ferry copies continuously between beats, and the tiles in Alpha receive doubled billing weight.'}
rationale: A ferry over 2 MB is sharded without automatic reordering, and eager mode doubles Beta's normal weight of four tiles times five beats from 20 to 40.

stem: A 2.6 MB record is sent through a ferry, and the receiving lane sometimes sees later sections before earlier sections. What is the most likely cause?
options: {'A': 'The ferry split the record into shards that can arrive out of order, and Tessellate did not reorder them.', 'B': 'The receiving lane exceeded seven tiles, causing Tessellate to reverse the record.', 'C': "A retry used the record's original input and rearranged its sections.", 'D': 'The metrics sampler omitted sections that arrived between sampled beats.'}
rationale: Ferries larger than 2 MB are split into shards that may arrive out of order, and Tessellate does not reorder them.

stem: A tile in a pinned lane has retry.limit set to 6 and first runs with input version 1. Immediately after its first failure, upstream data changes to version 2. What happens if the tile keeps failing?
options: {'A': 'Its retries use version 2 with normal back-off, and only the lane fails after the last retry.', 'B': 'Its retries alternate between versions 1 and 2, and the pin is removed after the last retry.', 'C': 'Its retries use version 1 without back-off, and the whole run fails if the tile remains failed.', 'D': 'Its retries use version 2 without back-off, and the tile is silently queued after the last retry.'}
rationale: Retries retain the original version 1 inputs, a limit above 5 disables back-off, and an ultimately failed tile in a pinned lane fails the whole run.

stem: A tile failed using an old upstream value, but the upstream value has now been corrected. The next execution must use the corrected value rather than the failed tile's saved input. What should the operator do?
options: {'A': 'Increase retry.limit so the next retry reloads upstream data.', 'B': 'Set ferry.eager to true before allowing the retry.', 'C': 'Compact the ledger and then resume the same retry sequence.', 'D': "Stop using that tile's retry sequence and launch a fresh tile execution after the correction."}
rationale: Every retry reuses the tile's original inputs, so a fresh tile execution is needed to obtain corrected upstream data.

stem: Four independent audit tiles must run on every beat for 30 beats, and their lane names must begin with an underscore. Which setup satisfies the requirement?
options: {'A': 'Place all four tiles in one pinned underscore lane and renew its pin after 12 beats.', 'B': 'Place all four tiles in one unpinned underscore lane and set retry.limit to 6.', 'C': 'Place the tiles in one ordinary unpinned lane so the scheduler can see them.', 'D': 'Split the tiles across two pinned underscore lanes with at most three tiles each, and renew both pins before they expire.'}
rationale: Underscore lanes must be pinned to run, pinned lanes hold at most three tiles, and their pins must be renewed because they expire after 12 beats.

stem: An underscore lane was pinned and ran normally, but it stopped after 12 beats even though no upgrade or configuration change occurred. What is the most likely explanation?
options: {'A': "The lane's pin expired because it was not renewed with pin.renew.", 'B': 'The scheduler rejected the lane because underscore lanes may run for only 12 beats.', 'C': 'The lane was automatically split because it contained more than 2 MB of data.', 'D': 'The ledger stopped the lane when its billing history reached 12 beats.'}
rationale: Pins expire after 12 beats unless they are renewed with pin.renew, and an underscore lane cannot run without a pin.

stem: A receiving lane has five tiles, including two idle tiles, and runs for six beats with ferry.eager set to true. Its billing weight is therefore 60. Which proposed change has the stated effect on billing weight?
options: {'A': 'Run ledger.compact, reducing the billing weight from 60 to 30.', 'B': 'Remove the two idle tiles while keeping the same beats and eager setting, reducing the billing weight from 60 to 36.', 'C': 'Split the lane into two lanes, guaranteeing that the billing weight falls below 60.', 'D': 'Delete the stored ledger history without changing the lane, reducing the billing weight to zero.'}
rationale: Removing the two idle tiles leaves three billed tiles, so eager billing becomes three tiles times six beats times two, or 36.

stem: Which operator statement about Tessellate billing is mistaken?
options: {'A': 'Idle tiles still count toward billing weight when their lane is running.', 'B': 'Running ledger.compact lowers billing weight by deleting old history.', 'C': 'An eager ferry doubles the billing weight of every tile in its receiving lane.', 'D': 'Merging two half-full lanes into one lane reduces billing weight.'}
rationale: ledger.compact reduces stored history but does not reduce billing weight.

stem: A normal unpinned lane already contains seven tiles, and an operator adds an eighth tile. What happens to the eighth tile?
options: {'A': 'It is silently queued rather than rejected.', 'B': 'It immediately runs in a newly created lane.', 'C': 'It replaces the oldest tile in the lane.', 'D': 'It is rejected with a lane-capacity error.'}
rationale: A lane holds at most seven tiles, and an eighth tile is silently queued.

stem: Six tiles must exchange data directly through shared memory with no ferry delay, and they must remain visible to the scheduler without pin renewal. Which layout meets these requirements?
options: {'A': 'Put three tiles in each of two ordinary lanes and rely on their memories being shared.', 'B': 'Put all six tiles in one pinned ordinary lane.', 'C': 'Put all six tiles in one ordinary, non-underscore, unpinned lane.', 'D': 'Put all six tiles in one unpinned underscore lane.'}
rationale: Six tiles fit within one normal lane's seven-tile capacity, share that lane's memory, and remain scheduler-visible without pinning.

stem: A gate is checked at the start of beat 8 and its condition is false. The condition becomes true two seconds later and remains true. When can the blocked tile first proceed?
options: {'A': 'Immediately when the condition becomes true', 'B': 'At the start of beat 9, when the gate is checked again', 'C': 'At the start of beat 13, when metrics are sampled', 'D': 'Only after the lane is pinned'}
rationale: Tessellate checks gates once per beat, so a condition that becomes true after the beat 8 check is not noticed until beat 9.

stem: A tile passed an approval gate before a snapshot was taken. After the snapshot is restored, the approval condition is currently false and the tile is blocked at the same gate again. What best explains this behavior?
options: {'A': 'Restoring a snapshot re-runs gates from scratch', 'B': 'Snapshots preserve ferry contents but discard gate names', 'C': 'Gates are permanently closed after twelve beats', 'D': 'The tile lost its lane permissions during the restore'}
rationale: A snapshot restore re-runs gates from scratch, so even a tile that previously passed a gate can block again.

stem: A reporting tile must read every lane, including `_audit`, but a payment tile must not receive that access. What is the least-access design if permissions are inherited from lanes?
options: {'A': 'Keep both tiles in one lane and grant `wide` only to the reporting tile', 'B': 'Keep both tiles in one lane and grant `wide` only to the payment tile', 'C': 'Put the reporting tile in a separate lane with `wide` scope and leave the payment tile in a lane without `wide`', 'D': 'Put both tiles in an underscore lane without granting `wide`'}
rationale: Because permissions are inherited from the lane, isolating the reporting tile in a `wide` lane avoids granting the payment tile unnecessary access.

stem: A lane contains four tiles, but only one needs to read every lane. An operator grants that tile `wide` scope while leaving it in the shared lane. Why is this grant over-broad?
options: {'A': "The `wide` scope also doubles the lane's billing weight", 'B': "All tiles in the lane inherit the lane's permissions and therefore gain the broad access", 'C': 'The `wide` scope automatically pins every lane', 'D': 'All underscore lanes become visible to the scheduler'}
rationale: Tessellate permissions are inherited from the lane, so the other three tiles cannot remain narrower than the tile receiving `wide` access.

stem: At snapshot time, lane Alpha's memory contains value X, lane Beta's memory contains value Y, and a ferry carrying value Z from Alpha to Beta is still in transit. What will the snapshot restore?
options: {'A': 'X, Y, and the in-transit ferry carrying Z', 'B': 'Only X because snapshots capture source lanes only', 'C': 'Only Z because ferry contents replace lane memory', 'D': 'X and Y, but not the in-transit ferry carrying Z'}
rationale: Snapshots capture lane memory but do not capture any ferry contents that are in transit.

stem: A source tile placed a record into a ferry and then deleted its local copy. A snapshot was taken while the record was still in transit, and the system was later restored from that snapshot. Why is the record absent after the restore?
options: {'A': 'The restore discarded all lane memory created before the snapshot', 'B': 'Ferries can only deliver records to pinned lanes', 'C': "The snapshot did not capture the ferry's in-transit record, and the local copy had already been deleted", 'D': 'Restoring a snapshot automatically compacts the ledger'}
rationale: The only remaining copy was inside the ferry, and snapshots do not include ferry contents in transit.

stem: An operator needs the candidate output produced immediately before a tile fails, but enabling `trace` records only the tile's inputs. Which approach can preserve that output for later inspection?
options: {'A': 'Write the candidate output into lane memory before reporting the failure, then take a snapshot after the write', 'B': 'Enable `trace` twice so that the second trace records outputs', 'C': 'Run `ledger.compact` immediately after the failure', 'D': 'Wait for the next metrics sample, which records all tile outputs'}
rationale: Since `trace` never records outputs, explicitly placing the output in lane memory allows a later snapshot to capture it.

stem: A brief failure event occurs during beat 14 and ends before beat 15. The metrics system samples at beats 5, 10, 15, and so on, and no metric for the event appears. What is the correct explanation?
options: {'A': 'Metrics are disabled for all unpinned lanes', 'B': 'Failures are recorded only when retry back-off is enabled', 'C': 'The beat 15 sample should contain every event since beat 10, so the absence proves a permission error', 'D': 'The event occurred between metric samples, and Tessellate does not record events between samples'}
rationale: Metrics are sampled only on every fifth beat, and events that begin and end between those samples are not recorded.

stem: A pinned underscore lane runs normally before a Tessellate version upgrade, but it stops running immediately afterward even though its configuration is otherwise unchanged. What should the operator do?
options: {'A': 'Increase the lane capacity to seven tiles', 'B': 'Re-establish the pin because upgrades reset all pins', 'C': 'Enable eager mode on a ferry connected to the lane', 'D': 'Restore the most recent snapshot to recover the pin'}
rationale: A Tessellate upgrade resets every pin, and an underscore lane will not run again until it is pinned.

stem: An operator adds `ferry.turbo` from documentation for a newer Tessellate release, but the current older version shows no error and behavior does not change. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: {'A': 'The setting is waiting for the next fifth-beat metrics sample', 'B': 'The setting works only in lanes containing seven tiles', 'C': 'The running version does not recognize the key and silently ignores it', 'D': 'The setting was stored inside an in-transit ferry'}
rationale: Tessellate silently ignores configuration keys that the running version does not recognize.

stem: An order-support agent sometimes issues refunds for ineligible orders because it calls an issue_refund tool using an amount inferred from the conversation. Which tool-design change is the best fix?
options: {'A': 'Make the refund service enforce eligibility and amount limits, and require the mutation tool to receive a short-lived authorization token produced by a validated eligibility check.', 'B': 'Add more examples of eligible refunds to the system prompt while leaving the refund tool unchanged.', 'C': 'Ask the model to explain its eligibility reasoning before every refund tool call.', 'D': 'Increase the model temperature so it considers more possible interpretations of the refund policy.'}
rationale: Business rules and authorization should be enforced at the tool boundary rather than entrusted to the model's reasoning.

stem: A shipping agent repeatedly passes package weights in pounds to a quote tool that interprets every numeric weight as kilograms. The tool schema defines weight only as a number, and its description does not mention units. Why is the tool being misused?
options: {'A': "The schema fails to specify the required unit or provide a unit field, leaving the model to guess the tool's convention.", 'B': 'The tool returns too many shipping services for the model to compare reliably.', 'C': 'The agent is unable to call tools that accept numeric arguments.', 'D': 'The quote tool should return its results as unstructured prose instead of structured data.'}
rationale: An ambiguous argument contract makes a unit mismatch likely, so the schema should encode or clearly state the required unit.

stem: An API reuses cached input only when the serialized prompt prefix is identical. An application places tool definitions before a large, unchanged reference manual, but it generates the tool-definition array by iterating over an unordered map. User questions appear after the manual. Why are cache hits unexpectedly rare?
options: {'A': 'Different user questions invalidate all earlier prompt tokens even when they occur after the cached prefix.', 'B': 'Nondeterministic ordering of the serialized tool definitions changes the prefix before the manual, preventing an exact prefix match.', 'C': 'Changing the output temperature necessarily creates a different cache entry for every request.', 'D': 'Cached prompts cannot contain tool definitions or reference documents.'}
rationale: Because caching depends on an identical serialized prefix, unstable tool ordering changes the prefix and prevents reuse of the following manual tokens.

stem: An application uses a prefix-based prompt cache and sends the same long policy manual with many different customer questions. Which prompt layout will usually minimize input cost?
options: {'A': 'Place each customer question first, followed by the policy manual and fixed instructions.', 'B': 'Interleave changing customer data throughout the policy manual to keep related details close together.', 'C': 'Place stable instructions and the policy manual first, then append customer-specific data and the current question.', 'D': 'Randomize the order of policy sections on each request so the model does not develop positional bias.'}
rationale: A long stable prefix can be reused across requests when changing customer content is placed after it.

stem: An agent reads untrusted web pages and can use tools that send email and modify customer records. Which design provides the strongest mitigation against indirect prompt injection from a web page?
options: {'A': 'Tell the model in the system prompt to ignore any instructions found in web pages.', 'B': 'Remove sentences containing phrases such as ignore previous instructions before sending pages to the model.', 'C': 'Put web-page text in a separate message while continuing to execute every well-formed tool call the model produces.', 'D': 'Treat page content as untrusted data, give the agent least-privilege tools, and require an independent policy layer to validate authorization, arguments, and user confirmation before consequential actions.'}
rationale: A privilege boundary with least-privilege tools and independent authorization limits damage even when injected content influences the model.

stem: A research agent retrieves a web page, asks a model to produce an action in JSON, and sends any schema-valid action directly to an executor that can transfer files outside the organization. Which pipeline step turns a prompt injection in the page into a privileged exploit?
options: {'A': 'The retriever downloads the page over HTTPS.', 'B': 'The model represents its proposed action as JSON.', 'C': 'The executor treats schema-valid model output as authorized and performs the external transfer without a separate policy check.', 'D': 'The application records the retrieved page in an audit log.'}
rationale: Schema validity does not establish authorization, so directly executing model-proposed actions allows injected instructions to trigger privileged effects.

stem: A team must compare two stochastic customer-service agents that can call tools and update accounts. Which evaluation method gives the most defensible estimate of which agent performs better?
options: {'A': 'Deploy each agent during a different month and compare raw complaint counts without adjusting for traffic or customer mix.', 'B': "Compare only whether each agent's tool calls are valid JSON, because syntactic validity represents end-to-end success.", 'C': 'Select ten examples on which the new agent looked strong during development and ask its developers to grade the outputs.', 'D': 'Run both agents repeatedly on the same representative held-out tasks, verify final state and prohibited side effects, use blinded adjudication where needed, and report paired uncertainty estimates.'}
